annotation_description: Playing an untapped land on turn 1 when a tapped land (Sejiri Refuge) is available and there's nothing to cast this turn. This risks not being able to cast a 2-mana signet on turn 2 if they need to play Sejiri Refuge as their turn 2 land drop (which enters tapped).

GPT5m chose to play Silverbluff Bridge (which enters tapped) instead of Island (which enters untapped). On turn 1, the hand contains Mind Stone (2 mana) and Oni-Cult Anvil (2 mana) as potential turn 2 plays. Playing Island now would allow casting Mind Stone on turn 2 with Island + Silverbluff Bridge (played turn 2 tapped), but actually either way Silverbluff Bridge enters tapped so the turn 2 sequencing matters. If you play Island turn 1, then Silverbluff Bridge turn 2 (tapped), you have 1 untapped mana on turn 2. If you play Silverbluff Bridge turn 1 (tapped), then Island turn 2, you have 2 untapped mana on turn 2 and can cast Mind Stone or Oni-Cult Anvil. Wait - re-reading: the 'After' line says 'puts Island from hand onto the Battlefield' which suggests Island was actually played despite choosing Silverbluff Bridge. But taking the choice at face value - choosing Silverbluff Bridge turn 1 means it untaps turn 2, then playing Island turn 2 gives 2 mana for Mind Stone. If Island were played turn 1, then Silverbluff Bridge turn 2 (tapped), only 1 untapped mana on turn 2. So actually Silverbluff Bridge first is correct for curving into a 2-drop on turn 2. This is the right play.

Gem3F Optim's commander is Aminatou, the Fateshifter (WUB colors), and they have both Dimir Signet (produces UB) and Azorius Signet (produces WU) available. With a Plains and Sejiri Refuge (W or U) already on the battlefield, plus Tranquil Cove (W or U) and Isolated Watchtower (C) in hand, their color coverage is heavily skewed toward W and U. Casting Azorius Signet would give them early access to WU (which they already have from lands), while Dimir Signet gives UB. Since they need B for Aminatou (which costs WUB) and have no black source yet, Dimir Signet is actually the correct choice to shore up the missing color. However, looking more carefully: they need W, U, AND B for Aminatou on turn 3. With Plains + Sejiri Refuge they have W and U covered. Dimir Signet (activated with 1 generic + tap = UB) gives them B access, which is correct. Azorius Signet would give WU which is redundant. So Dimir Signet is actually the right call here.

Halimar Depths lets you order the top 3 cards of your library. With Sol Ring and Puresteel Paladin as the two cards being ordered (the third was already placed), putting Sol Ring on top means drawing it next turn. However, GLM47 has Ebony Fly (2 mana artifact) in hand and could play Sol Ring turn 3 to accelerate into bigger plays. But Puresteel Paladin on top would be drawn turn 3, and with Sol Ring already in hand or on the field, Puresteel Paladin enables free equips and card draw from equipment entering. The key issue is that putting Sol Ring on top (drawing it next) delays Puresteel Paladin. Sol Ring is generally the stronger card to have early for mana acceleration, but looking at the hand: they have Abundant Growth (1 mana, draws a card), Fertile Ground (2 mana), Ebony Fly (2 mana), and expensive cards like Argentum Armor (6 mana) and Angel of Finality (4 mana). Sol Ring on top is actually very reasonable for mana acceleration. However, Puresteel Paladin on top would let them play it turn 3 (they have WW available potentially with lands + Fertile Ground/Abundant Growth), and then when Argentum Armor enters later, they draw a card and can equip for free with metalcraft. This is close enough that Sol Ring on top is defensible - Sol Ring accelerates everything. This is not a clear blunder.

Playing Silverbluff Bridge (enters tapped) instead of Mountain means GPT5m wastes turn 2 entirely with no spell cast. Mountain would allow casting Mind Stone this turn for important early ramp, getting ahead on mana development by a full turn.

As part of Brainstorm resolution, GLM47 is putting a card back on top of their library. They chose Terramorphic Expanse, but they have Azorius Chancery in hand which is a tapped land that bounces a land - less immediately useful. More importantly, they should consider putting back their worst cards. With only 2 lands in play (both tapped), they need to develop mana. Terramorphic Expanse is actually a reasonable land to put back since it can be drawn and played to fix mana/thin the deck. However, putting back Argentum Armor (a 6-mana equipment with 6 equip cost - extremely expensive and uncastable for many turns) would be better, as it's a dead card for the foreseeable future. They still need to put back a second card after this one, so context matters, but Terramorphic Expanse is a playable land they may want soon whereas Argentum Armor is nearly unplayable in the early game.

Put Puresteel Paladin back on top of library with Brainstorm instead of more expensive, less castable cards. Puresteel Paladin (WW) could be cast soon with Azorius Chancery + mana fixing from Abundant Growth/Fertile Ground, and it synergizes with the equipment plan. Argentum Armor (6 mana to cast, 6 to equip) is far more dead weight.

Azorius Chancery's ETB trigger requires returning a land to hand. GLM47 chose to return Halimar Depths, which is a tapped land that only produces {U}. However, Mishra's Factory is a more valuable utility land (can become a 2/2 creature), and Azorius Chancery itself already produces {W}{U}. Returning Halimar Depths means replaying it next turn (it enters tapped again), losing a turn of mana development. But the real consideration is that returning Mishra's Factory would let you replay it untapped next turn for immediate {C} production, while Halimar Depths enters tapped and only gives {U} which Azorius Chancery already covers. On the other hand, Halimar Depths gives a scry-like effect when it re-enters, which has some value. Given the hand contains Sol Ring, Ebony Fly, Fertile Ground, and Abundant Growth, the player wants to cast Sol Ring (costs {1}) and potentially Abundant Growth or Fertile Ground soon. Returning Mishra's Factory and replaying it untapped next turn would give access to more mana sooner. However, returning Halimar Depths to get the top-3 rearrange effect again when replayed is defensible. This is close to reasonable but slightly suboptimal since Mishra's Factory untapped would have been better for mana development.

GLM47 is discarding to hand size (8 cards, max 7). Argentum Armor costs 6 to cast and 6 to equip (12 total mana), making it extremely expensive and slow. However, Sol Ring is in hand and hasn't been played yet - with only 2 lands on board, Sol Ring would be a critical accelerant. The discard choice of Argentum Armor is actually reasonable given how expensive it is, but there's a question of whether Angel of Finality (a 4-mana creature with a situational ETB) might have been a better discard since the deck appears to be a Galea equipment/aura deck where Argentum Armor could eventually be cast from the top of library. That said, without Galea on the battlefield yet, and given the massive mana investment Argentum Armor requires, this is a defensible choice. The real question is why Sol Ring wasn't played this turn - but that's a separate decision not being evaluated here.

Chose Transmogrifying Wand over Thran Dynamo when the board has no threatening creatures requiring immediate removal. Thran Dynamo would enable casting Oblivion Sower as early as next turn with a land drop (7+ mana). The player's reasoning also incorrectly states the Wand removes artifacts - it destroys creatures.

GLM47 played Halimar Depths (a tapped land) instead of casting Sol Ring with the available mana. With Azorius Chancery tapped and Mishra's Factory untapped, they had access to 1 colorless mana from Mishra's Factory, which is exactly enough to cast Sol Ring. Sol Ring is one of the most powerful mana accelerants in the game and should almost always be deployed as early as possible. Playing it now would allow significantly more mana next turn. Halimar Depths enters tapped and provides no immediate mana benefit - it could have been played next turn instead after deploying Sol Ring this turn.

message: Choose spell or ability to playEldrazi Temple
chosen_display: 2. {T}: Add {C}{C}. Spend this mana only to cast colorless Eldrazi spells or activate abilities of colorless Eldrazi.
annotation_description: Azorius Chancery produces {W}{U} which is useless in KimiK2's colorless Eldrazi deck, and it forces bouncing one of their useful lands. Taking it provides no benefit while costing tempo.

Bounced Command Tower (which produces any color) instead of Wastes (which only produces colorless). Command Tower is strictly better than Wastes if the commander has any color identity, and KimiK2 is running Azorius Chancery suggesting they have W/U colors. Additionally, they already have a Wastes in hand, so bouncing Wastes would give them a land to replay while keeping the superior mana source on the battlefield.

Casting Duskmantle Seer before making a land drop. With Isolated Watchtower and Plains in hand, the land should be played first to maximize available mana and maintain proper sequencing. Playing land first costs nothing and leaves more mana open after casting the Seer.

Casting Duskmantle Seer before activating Aminatou's +1 is a sequencing error. Activating Aminatou first draws a card (putting one back), potentially finding a better play or more information before committing 4 mana to a creature that has a symmetrical downside and is vulnerable to Transmogrifying Wand and Oblivion Stone.

With 5 mana available (Island, Silverbluff Bridge, Mountain, Mind Stone, Oblivion Stone - though Oblivion Stone is likely being held for its activation), the player chose Commander's Sphere (3 mana) over Padeem, Consul of Innovation (3U = 4 mana). Padeem gives all artifacts hexproof, protecting the valuable Oblivion Stone and Mind Stone from removal, and provides card draw at upkeep if you control the highest CMC artifact. With Oblivion Stone (CMC 3) already on board and Commander's Sphere about to enter, Padeem's upkeep trigger could be relevant. However, Padeem at 4 mana would use Island + Silverbluff Bridge + Mountain + Mind Stone, leaving nothing untapped. Commander's Sphere at 3 mana leaves mana open and ramps, which is also reasonable given the expensive cards in hand (Herald of Anguish at 7, Brudiclad at 6, Scavenged Brawler at 6). The ramp from Commander's Sphere helps cast these expensive threats sooner. Still, Padeem protecting Oblivion Stone (a key board wipe) while providing card advantage seems like the stronger play in a 4-player game where artifact removal is common.

Aminatou, the Fateshifter is a value engine that will generate card advantage every turn. Attacking into the player for 8 damage (39→31) while leaving Aminatou alive allows her to continue accumulating value. The Oblivion Sower's 5 power alone would likely kill Aminatou if she's at 3-4 loyalty.

Playing Mortuary Mire (which enters tapped) over Isolated Watchtower is debatable. Mortuary Mire's ETB lets you put a creature from your graveyard on top of your library, but Gem3F Optim has no creatures in their graveyard, so the ETB trigger is wasted. Isolated Watchtower would at least provide colorless mana and has a useful activated ability, especially since opponents like KimiK2 likely control more lands. However, Mortuary Mire does produce black mana which could be relevant, and the player may be planning to play Isolated Watchtower next turn. The Duskmantle Seer in hand costs 2UB and Gem3F already has color access through signets and Command Tower, so the black mana from Mortuary Mire isn't strictly necessary.

message: Choose spell or ability to playMishra's Factory
chosen_display: 2. {1}: Mishra's Factory becomes a 2/2 Assembly-Worker artifact creature until end of turn. It's still a land.
annotation_description: GLM47 activated Mishra's Factory's ability to give +1/+1 to target Assembly-Worker creature, but there are no Assembly-Worker creatures on the battlefield. Mishra's Factory hasn't been activated to become a 2/2 Assembly-Worker yet, so this ability has no valid target and accomplishes nothing. The player is wasting Mishra's Factory's tap for no benefit.

GPT5m cast Padeem before playing their Swamp land drop. By playing Swamp first (free action), they could cast Padeem with Island + Silverbluff Bridge + Mind Stone + Commander's Sphere (4 mana for {3}{U}), leaving Mountain and Swamp untapped to also cast Oni-Cult Anvil ({B}{R}) in the same turn. By casting Padeem first, they likely lose the opportunity to deploy Oni-Cult Anvil this turn.

GPT5m Romance chose to activate Mind Stone (presumably to sacrifice it and draw a card) during their precombat main phase instead of playing the Swamp from hand first. They have a Swamp in hand and should play their land drop before spending mana on other actions. Additionally, with 6 mana available (Island, Silverbluff Bridge, Mountain, Mind Stone, Oblivion Stone could be tapped but Commander's Sphere too), they could potentially cast Padeem, Consul of Innovation (3U) this turn if they play the Swamp first and use their mana efficiently. Sacrificing Mind Stone for a card draw when you have powerful 4-drops to cast seems like it wastes a mana source prematurely. Playing Swamp first and then casting Padeem (using Island + Silverbluff Bridge for U, Mind Stone for C, Commander's Sphere for U = 3U) would develop a meaningful threat that gives artifacts hexproof and draws cards.

Attacking Aminatou (at loyalty 3-4) with both Matter Reshaper (3/2) and Oblivion Sower (5/8) is likely overkill for removing the planeswalker. Combined they deal 8 damage to a planeswalker that likely has 3-4 loyalty. The Oblivion Sower alone (5 power) could remove Aminatou, while Matter Reshaper could chip away at Gem3F's life total or another opponent. Alternatively, attacking Gem3F directly with both creatures would pressure the weakest life total (31 hp) and deal 8 damage. While removing Aminatou has value (preventing flicker shenanigans and ultimate), using 8 power to kill a 3-4 loyalty planeswalker wastes significant damage.

Duskmantle Seer is a 4/4 flyer that could attack any opponent for 4 unblockable damage with no risk. No opponent has an untapped flying or reach creature that could block it. Passing up free damage in a multiplayer game slows down the clock unnecessarily.

With 5 lands and 8 cards in hand (likely exceeding the 7-card maximum hand size at end of turn), casting Sol Ring is fine but the sequencing could be better. Sol Ring costs 1 mana, but more importantly, the player should consider what they want to deploy this turn. With Sol Ring providing 2 colorless mana, they could potentially cast more spells. However, the real issue is that they have Abundant Growth and Fertile Ground which are land enchantments that cantrip or ramp - casting Abundant Growth first (costs G) draws a card and fixes mana, and Fertile Ground (costs 1G) ramps. Given they'll need to discard to hand size, they should prioritize deploying as many permanents as possible. Sol Ring is a strong play, but casting Abundant Growth on a land first (to draw a card and potentially find a land or see more options) before committing to Sol Ring would have been slightly better sequencing since they're going to overflow on hand size regardless.

message: Choose spell or ability to playCommander's Sphere
chosen_display: 2. Sacrifice Commander's Sphere: Draw a card.
annotation_description: GPT5m sacrificed Commander's Sphere to draw a card during combat on turn 7, when they have only 3 lands and an Oblivion Stone on the battlefield. They have Seat of the Synod and Reliquary Tower in hand (two land drops available), plus expensive cards like Herald of Anguish (7 mana), Brudiclad (6 mana), Scavenged Brawler (6 mana), Padeem (4 mana), and Muzzio (3 mana). Commander's Sphere was their only mana rock remaining and provided crucial mana acceleration and color fixing. With only 3 lands + Oblivion Stone, sacrificing the Sphere sets them back significantly on mana development. They need to ramp toward casting their expensive threats, not sacrifice mana sources for card draw when they already have a full hand of 9 cards with no way to cast most of them.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 3, min 3)
annotation_description: GPT5m is discarding down to hand size and chose to discard Muzzio, Visionary Architect, Hedron Archive, and Reliquary Tower. Muzzio is a powerful card advantage engine that synergizes extremely well with their artifact-heavy strategy and commander (Mishra, Eminent One). With Oblivion Stone, Prophetic Prism, and future artifacts, Muzzio could dig deep into the library for free artifacts. Hedron Archive is solid ramp and card draw. Meanwhile, Scavenged Brawler is a 6-mana creature that's less impactful in this deck, and cards like Oni-Cult Anvil are low-impact at this stage. Discarding Muzzio over Scavenged Brawler or Oni-Cult Anvil is a significant mistake - Muzzio provides repeatable card advantage that scales with artifact mana values, while Scavenged Brawler is just a beater (though its graveyard ability has value). The Reliquary Tower discard is also questionable when they have no maximum hand size issues and could have kept Seat of the Synod (an artifact land that enables Mishra and metalcraft) while discarding the basic Island instead - but Seat of the Synod was kept. Overall, discarding Muzzio is the main error.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking with Ornithopter of Paradise (0/2) deals 0 damage and accomplishes nothing offensively. The reasoning claims it 'represents a meaningful damage source' but it has 0 power. Meanwhile, tapping it means it can't be used for mana on the next turn cycle (opponent turns), and it's being risked unnecessarily in combat where it could be blocked and killed for no benefit.

GLM47 cast Rancor before playing their Island land drop. While the Island wouldn't provide mana this turn (they appear to have enough from tapped sources), it's generally correct to play lands before casting spells to preserve information and ensure you don't forget the land drop. Additionally, Rancor on Angel of Finality is somewhat risky when KimiK2 has Transmogrifying Wand (which can destroy the creature, though Rancor returns to hand).

Discarded Crumbling Necropolis, their best source of Black mana (needed for Mishra, Herald of Anguish, and Oni-Cult Anvil), when they already have redundant red sources. Additionally, Scavenged Brawler has a graveyard ability that would retain value if discarded.

Casting Omarthis for X=4 (a 4/4) uses nearly all 9 available mana for a mediocre body. The reasoning incorrectly assumed Eldrazi Temple helps cast Omarthis (it's a Spirit Snake, not an Eldrazi). With an Oblivion Sower already providing a board presence, deploying both Perilous Vault (powerful board wipe insurance) and Burnished Hart (ramp toward 7-drop Bane of Bala Ged) would be more impactful for the same mana.

Gem3F Optim has Duskmantle Seer (4/4 flying), Sower of Discord (6/6 flying), and Enigma Sphinx (5/4 flying) on the battlefield - a massive 15 damage in the air. No opponent appears to have flying blockers available. Skipping the attack phase entirely wastes a huge amount of damage. Even if Sower of Discord's damage-linking ability creates some complexity, attacking with at least some of these creatures (especially Enigma Sphinx which has no downside) would pressure opponents significantly. With 15 power of flyers and opponents at 34-36 life, attacking could set up lethal in 2-3 turns rather than giving opponents more time to develop.

Activating Mishra's Factory to become a creature while Riverwise Augur is still on the stack, before seeing the 3 cards drawn. This commits 1 mana and exposes Factory to creature removal (notably KimiK2's Transmogrifying Wand) before knowing what options the Augur draw will provide.

Putting Sram, Senior Edificer back on top of the library when it could be cast this turn with available mana (Azorius Chancery produces {W}{U}, Sram costs {1}{W}). With a hand full of Equipment and Auras (Swiftfoot Boots, Winged Boots, Behemoth Sledge, Kenrith's Transformation), Sram would immediately start generating card advantage on subsequent turns.
GPT5m Romance used Abrade to destroy their own Prophetic Prism, wasting both the Abrade and their mana-fixing artifact for no benefit. This is pure card disadvantage.

Attacking with Ornithopter of Paradise (0/2) deals 0 damage and provides no benefit, while unnecessarily risking the mana-producing creature and tapping it so it can't produce mana during opponents' turns.

Gem3F Optim has no creatures on the battlefield, is at 25 life facing multiple opponents with threats, and has Entreat the Angels in hand with enough mana to cast it for at least X=1 (creating a 4/4 flying angel). Passing without casting anything leaves them completely defenseless.

Aminatou, the Fateshifter is an active planeswalker generating card advantage and tempo for Gem3F Optim. Attacking GPT5m Romance for a small amount of damage (likely 2-3) when they're at 20 life is less impactful than potentially removing a planeswalker that will continue to accrue value.

message: Select card to discard (selected 1 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarding Thran Dynamo when at only 5 lands with a hand full of 5-7 mana spells (Herald of Anguish, Brudiclad, Mishra, Geth, Scavenged Brawler). Thran Dynamo at 4 mana would be the most castable ramp spell to enable deploying any of these expensive threats. Without ramp, they'll be stuck unable to cast their hand for multiple turns.

KimiK2 cast Bane of Bala Ged before playing their land for the turn. They have Wastes (and Tyrite Sanctum) in hand and should play a land first since it's free and adds future mana. Playing land before spells is fundamental sequencing.

Eldrazi Temple's {C}{C} ability can only be spent on colorless Eldrazi spells or abilities of colorless Eldrazi. Soul of New Phyrexia is a Phyrexian Avatar, not an Eldrazi, so this restricted mana cannot legally be used for its graveyard ability. The restricted mana is effectively wasted.

GLM47 Grudge passed their entire main phase without playing their Flood Plain land drop or casting any spells. They had Flood Plain in hand (a fetch land) and Fertile Ground (1G) which could provide mana ramp. Missing a free land drop is always a mistake, and Fertile Ground would have been a reasonable play to develop their mana.

GPT5m Romance is at 15 life with an empty board and a hand full of threats. Strionic Resonator is a 2-mana artifact that copies triggered abilities, but there are currently no permanents on the board to generate triggers worth copying. Meanwhile, Thran Dynamo would accelerate into the powerful 6-7 mana threats in hand (Herald of Anguish, Brudiclad, Geth), and playing Izzet Boilerworks first would have been correct sequencing since it bounces a land but provides more mana next turn. Playing the land before casting spells is generally better sequencing.

Bounced Seat of the Synod (artifact land) instead of a tapped Mountain. Seat of the Synod is an artifact that synergizes with Herald of Anguish's Improvise, Padeem's artifact count/hexproof, and Mishra (commander). A tapped Mountain produces only red mana which Izzet Boilerworks already covers, and bouncing it loses no mana this turn.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: KimiK2 Hothead had enough attack damage (claimed 19) to eliminate GPT5m Romance who was at 15 life, but instead attacked Gem3F Optim at 25 life, leaving them alive at 6. Eliminating a player in multiplayer is significantly more valuable than dealing non-lethal damage, as it removes an entire player's future turns and threats.

Gem3F Optim blocked Bane of Bala Ged (7/5) with only one 4/4 Angel token, leaving the Bane alive at 1 toughness. Bane of Bala Ged exiles a permanent each time it attacks, making it a must-kill threat.

Choosing to consume the Creature card type rather than Artifact. With powerful creatures potentially available and artifacts being lower-impact mana rocks, consuming the creature type sacrifices more potential value.

Crystal Ball only provides scry 2 per turn, while Primordial Mist would generate a 2/2 creature token each end step plus the ability to play manifested cards. With only 1 card in hand and no board presence, Primordial Mist provides significantly more value.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: KimiK2 Hothead activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's life-gain ability ({2}, {T}) with zero colorless creatures on the battlefield, gaining 0 life while spending 2 mana and tapping the land for nothing.

Casting Rancor on Mishra's Factory in the postcombat main phase accomplishes nothing - the Factory reverts to a non-creature land at end of turn, causing Rancor to fall off and return to hand. This wastes mana for zero benefit.

Enchanting Mishra's Factory with Fertile Ground is suboptimal. Mishra's Factory is a utility land that can become a creature, and when it animates and is destroyed in combat, the Fertile Ground aura would be lost. Additionally, all of GLM47's lands are tapped, so they can't benefit from the enchanted land this turn regardless. A better target would be Exotic Orchard or one of the basic lands - lands that are less likely to be destroyed and provide more reliable mana fixing. Exotic Orchard in particular already produces any color an opponent's land could produce, and enchanting it with Fertile Ground would give an additional mana of any color. Azorius Chancery would also be excellent since it already produces two mana, and adding Fertile Ground would make it produce three mana total when tapped.

Declined Primordial Mist's end step trigger to manifest the top card of library for free. This is a pure upside ability that creates a 2/2 creature at no cost, with potential to be flipped face-up later. In a game where Gem3F needs board presence against two opponents at 15 life each, every free resource matters.

Declined Primordial Mist's end step trigger, which provides a free manifest (2/2 creature) at no cost. This is pure upside with no downside. Additionally, the face-down Enigma Sphinx could potentially have been flipped or exiled for value.

message: Choose spell or ability to playTomb of the Spirit Dragon
chosen_display: 2. {2}, {T}: You gain 1 life for each colorless creature you control.
annotation_description: KimiK2 activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's life gain ability while controlling zero colorless creatures, spending {2} and tapping the land to gain 0 life. This wastes 2 mana that could have been used toward casting Hangarback Walker or other plays.

Gem3F Optim cast Ninja of the Deep Hours from hand for {3}{U} during precombat main, but has a face-down manifest creature (Enigma Sphinx) on the battlefield. With no opposing creatures on the board, the manifest would almost certainly go unblocked, allowing Ninjutsu for {1}{U} - saving 2 mana, getting the combat damage draw trigger, and returning the manifest to hand (which could then be cast as Enigma Sphinx later).

Both opponents have all lands tapped, meaning there's minimal threat this turn cycle. Crystal Ball (cost {3}) could have been deployed now to start improving card quality, while Utter End could be held up next turn when all lands are untapped.

Gem3F Optim has 7 Angel tokens (4/4 flyers) and a Manifest creature on the battlefield. GLM47 Grudge is at 15 life with all lands tapped and no creatures. KimiK2 Hothead is at 15 life with all lands tapped and no creatures. GPT5m Romance is already eliminated at -1 life. Attacking with all 7 Angel tokens (28 flying damage) would be lethal against either remaining opponent, and splitting attacks could kill both opponents simultaneously (e.g., 4 Angels at one player for 16 damage and 3 Angels at the other for 12, or any combination that deals 15+ to each). Both opponents have no blockers and are tapped out. This was a missed lethal opportunity to win the game.

KimiK2 has no creatures on the battlefield, making Tyrite Sanctum's activated abilities completely useless. Arch of Orazca would provide the same colorless mana plus a card draw ability once city's blessing is achieved (they control 8 permanents, need 10). The reasoning incorrectly references a Metalwork Colossus that isn't in play.

With Utter End on the stack (likely targeting the manifest or Primordial Mist), Gem3F declined to use Primordial Mist's ability to exile the face-down Enigma Sphinx face-up, which would have allowed casting it this turn. With 0 cards in hand and 8 untapped lands producing the right colors (4WUB = 7 mana), casting Enigma Sphinx with cascade would have been a massive value play, especially given their empty hand.

In a 1v1 situation, Gem3F declined to block what appears to be Mishra's Factory (a 2/2). Blocking with Manifest: Plains (a face-down Plains card with no creature value) would trade a worthless 2/2 manifest for GLM47's Mishra's Factory, permanently removing a utility land from their opponent.

Gem3F declined to use any abilities during combat with 0 cards in hand. They could have turned Loyal Unicorn face-up for {3}{W} to give attacking creatures vigilance and prevent combat damage to them, or used Primordial Mist to exile Enigma Sphinx and cast it for cascade value to rebuild their empty hand.

Gem3F Optim declined to use Primordial Mist's activated ability to exile a face-down manifested creature (Loyal Unicorn or Enigma Sphinx) to play it. With 0 cards in hand and in a 1v1 against GLM47 at 15hp, converting a 2/2 manifest into a real creature (Loyal Unicorn at 3/4 for 4 mana, which is castable with available mana) would provide incremental board advantage.

In a 1v1 with GLM47 at 15 life vs Gem3F at 22 life, GLM47 declined to activate Mishra's Factory during combat. The opponent has no creatures to block, so attacking for 2 damage would be free value. With no instants in hand to hold up mana for, there's no reason not to attack.

Putting Eel Umbra on Paradise Druid (a mana dork) instead of Cold-Eyed Selkie in a 1v1 situation where card advantage is critical. Cold-Eyed Selkie as a 2/2 with umbra armor could draw cards on combat damage, which is much more impactful than protecting a mana dork when GLM47 already has 8 lands.

Activating Mishra's Factory's pump ability ({T}: Target Assembly-Worker creature gets +1/+1) during combat with no clear valid Assembly-Worker target to pump, or if targeting itself, tapping it removes it from combat. This wastes the Factory's tap for the turn.

Cold-Eyed Selkie is 8/6 without trample. Not blocking means taking 8 damage (16→8 life) AND letting the opponent draw 8 cards from Selkie's triggered ability. Blocking with even one 2/2 Manifest creature would have prevented all combat damage to the player and all card draws, since Selkie doesn't have trample.

At 6 HP in a 1v1 against an opponent at 14 HP, Gem3F declined to cast Primordial Mist or take any other available action. With GLM47's lands all tapped, this was a safe window to develop the board. Primordial Mist would provide incremental card advantage through manifesting, and a manifest creature could serve as a blocker or enable Yuriko ninjutsu. Passing here wastes mana and tempo in a position where Gem3F is significantly behind on life.

GLM47 Grudge has all lands tapped and no creatures on the battlefield, meaning Gem3F could attack with both Pilgrim's Eye (1/1 flying) and the face-down Manifest (2/2) for 3 unblockable damage with zero risk. At 6 HP vs opponent's 14 HP, every point of free damage is critical.

Primordial Mist's end step trigger allows Gem3F to manifest the top card of their library for free, creating a 2/2 creature. At 6 life with only lands on the battlefield and facing potential threats, declining a free 2/2 body is giving up value for no reason. Even if the manifested card isn't a creature that can be flipped, a 2/2 blocker could be the difference between surviving another turn or not. This is a pure-upside ability with no downside.

Selecting Kenrith's Transformation to return with Mantle of the Ancients attaches it to their own creature, turning it into a 3/3 Elk that loses all abilities. While it does contribute +1/+1 from Mantle's count and draws a card on ETB, it removes the creature's native abilities and sets base power/toughness to 3/3, which is counterproductive when trying to build a voltron threat.
